ORIGIN.quote: What the names *do* indicate is that the agents believed themselves to be Anthropic research agents and chose to say so — consistent with a scaffold whose system prompt frames the model as a research assistant. Confidence: **Medium-High** that these are genuinely Anthropic-model agents (name self-attribution + Claude-typical prose + AWS egress); **Low** that any specific named identity is meaningful
ORIGIN.reason: A reader comes away in no doubt that the report's own assessment is that these were genuinely Anthropic (Claude) agents running a large parallel eval campaign — the report weighs the naming evidence, rejects it as authentication, and then still assigns Medium-High confidence to Anthropic provenance. It falls short of 1.0 because it explicitly declines to commit on the operator side ("Medium on which harness/operator"), so it names Anthropic as the likely source of the models without concluding that the swarm was an Anthropic-run deployment.
